back: A parasite living on the outside of its host, e.g. ticks, lice, mites, fleas, biting flies.
A tick whose larva, nymph and adult all feed on the same animal (e.g. blue tick).
A tick whose larva, nymph and adult each feed on a different host, moulting on the ground (e.g. brown ear tick, bont tick).

front: Diseases spread by the blue tick
Diseases spread by the brown ear tick and the bont tick
back: Brown ear tick: theileriosis (January disease). Bont tick: heartwater.

front: Life cycle of the blue tick
back: Engorged female drops and lays eggs → larvae climb grass → attach to host → moult to nymph and adult on the same host → female engorges (about 3 weeks) and drops.

front: Six damages caused by external parasites
back: Blood loss, irritation, damaged hides, damaged teats, disease transmission, lower production.
Plunge dip, spray race, hand spraying, pour-ons, tick grease, pasture spelling, tick-resistant breeds.

front: Why keep dip wash at full strength?
back: A weak wash leaves survivors and leads to acaricide resistance.
